rationale: Evidence from iteration 1: still 0 finishes in 60 trials. Progress rose on the oval (0.37 mean, up from 0.12) and s-bend (0.25, up from 0.14), but line_loss_events remained 1.0 in every trial and max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.064, just past the 0.06 m limit. Steering oscillation rose to 0.24 on the oval and 0.21 on the s-bend, above the 0.2 level the Evaluator flagged. The Evaluator's rule for oscillation is to lower kp to about 3.0 first. Its rule for persistent line loss with max_error above 0.06 is to lower base_speed to 1.2 and keep kp at 3.5. I applied both in one step, because the two symptoms appeared together and the team needs a clean-to-off-track answer within the remaining iterations. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.4 to 1.2, to give the robot more time to correct on the bends and reduce the line loss. (2) kp 3.5 to 3.0, to cut the oscillation seen on the oval and s-bend. kd stays at 0.3 and ki at 0.1, both as in iteration 1. Geometry and sensor_weights are unchanged. I kept sensor_size at 0.016 so that the only changes are the controller's speed and gain. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and lower steering_oscillation (below 0.2 on all tracks). Completion within 3 s is unlikely at 1.2, so progress is the main score lever for now. Hypotheses to test: (a) line_loss_events falls toward 0 at base_speed 1.2; (b) steering_oscillation drops below 0.2 at kp 3.0; (c) max_error falls below 0.06 on the oval. Falsification: if line loss stays at 1.0 at base_speed 1.2, the cause is probably geometry (the 5-sensor span is 0.08 m, so the robot leaves the sensed area at about 0.06 m offset, the same as the off-track limit) and sensor placement or spacing should change next. If the robot is clean but completion_time is above 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 while keeping kp near 3.0.
